drugRefs.duration: 14-21 days if HSV confirmed (stop if CSF PCR negative and alternative diagnosis found)
drugRefs.why: Empiric acyclovir is mandatory for any encephalitis of unclear cause, since untreated HSV encephalitis carries very high mortality and treatment delay measurably worsens outcomes; the drug is well-tolerated even if HSV is ultimately excluded.

drugRefs.regimenLabel: Ceftriaxone + Vancomycin (empiric bacterial coverage pending CSF results)
drugRefs.dose: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q12h + Vancomycin 15-20 mg/kg IV q8-12h
drugRefs.why: Added because bacterial meningoencephalitis can present similarly and the consequences of missing it are severe; discontinued once CSF studies make bacterial infection unlikely.

drugRefs.regimenLabel: Doxycycline (if rickettsial/scrub typhus suspected — endemic, seasonal)
drugRefs.coverage: Added in endemic regions/seasons if scrub typhus or other rickettsial encephalitis is a clinical consideration, since this is treatable and easily missed.

coverageMatrix.completeness: Combination empiric therapy covers the major treatable causes pending CSF PCR and serology.
gaps: Arboviral encephalitides (e.g., Japanese encephalitis) have no specific antimicrobial therapy — management is supportive once confirmed, but empiric coverage of treatable causes should not be withheld while awaiting confirmation.

stewardship.deescalation: If CSF HSV PCR is negative and bacterial cultures are negative with a CSF profile inconsistent with bacterial infection, discontinue both acyclovir and antibacterial agents and pursue alternative diagnoses (autoimmune, arboviral, etc.).

framework: Do not withhold empiric acyclovir while awaiting CSF HSV PCR — the risk-benefit strongly favors early empiric treatment given HSV encephalitis mortality if delayed.
Discontinue empiric antibacterial coverage promptly once CSF findings make bacterial infection unlikely (e.g., lymphocytic pleocytosis, normal glucose, negative Gram stain/culture).
Stop acyclovir if CSF HSV PCR is negative and an alternative diagnosis is identified, rather than completing a full course by default.
